summary: Exhaustive forward/reverse walk completed. Instruction plus session-contract.md make CLI, event-time sessions, lateness, journal/restart, rejects, catalog gap overlay, and warehouse leave-alone discoverable and mostly tested. Reject classes are identified by event_id, not detail tokens. Blocking gap: last_run.warehouse.event_count and ops-report.inventory.event_count are published as COUNT(*) of click_event in catalog.sqlite, but the verifier only checks that the two integers match, are positive, and catalog.available is true, so a hardcoded matching pair still passes.

evidence.observation: Two paragraphs: incident (wrong closes, mixed tenants, duplicate side output, backward watermark) and repair of the Python processor via run-sessions; binds session-contract.md; names CLI flags, processor.json, journal, outputs, last_run.json, ops-report.json, catalog overlay, and leave-warehouse.

Binding CLI/paths/event schema/gap/duration/watermark/lateness/journal/restart/idempotency/empty/rejects. last_run.warehouse.event_count and ops-report.inventory.event_count must equal COUNT(*) of click_event; ops-report.catalog.available is true when catalog loaded. Enterprise catalog tenants overlay session_gap_ms=45000; other catalog plans keep processor.json.

Operator incident note: mixed-tenant u1, late 85000 after 100000 treated on-time, 1000ms straggler missing from late.jsonl, --reset-output wiping journal, seq stuck at 1. Points to contract and CLI; not a module repair map.
Current-state log corroborates on-time misclassification of f3/f4, journal rewrite seq=1, --reset-output clearing journal, unknown flag creating journal.
Public knobs session_gap_ms=30000, allowed_lateness_ms=10000, max_session_duration_ms=3600000; mutated by F2P config tests.
Operator entrypoint execs python3 -m src.cli; P2P asserts python3 remains.
click_event table is the catalog inventory the COUNT(*) contract names; catalog.sqlite is generated into /app/sessions/warehouse at image build and transferred with artifacts [/app/sessions].
t01 plan=enterprise is solver-visible; discovers the catalog overlay fixture tenant without leaking hidden event times.

40 tests: 25 F2P / 15 P2P by name. CLI exit-2, empty/zero-event, gap/holdout, input time-sort, tenant isolation, journal seq/prefix/nondecreasing/negative watermark, too-late schema, idempotent digests, restart, config gap/lateness, feed order, reset-output, plus P2P late-allowed, duration, warehouse SHA/10k, python CLI, contract formula string, reject event_id classes, ops field presence, enterprise overlay. test_p2p_ops_report_uses_warehouse_catalog does not query catalog.sqlite COUNT(*).

After a successful --input run, asserts last_run.json and ops-report.json exist, int(warehouse.event_count)==int(inventory.event_count), that value > 0, and catalog.available is True. No sqlite COUNT(*) comparison.
Reject classes identified by event_id (m1, empty string, m3) and accepted m4; asserts REJECT_MALFORMED and that those ids are absent from late.jsonl. Does not grade detail token spelling.
Three different users, one event each, identical event_time_ms. Permutation stability cannot observe (tenant_id, user_id, event_id) secondary order.
Used only for F2P/P2P classification labels. Coverage claims in the map were not treated as evidence.

PASS requires complete matrices and empty BLOCKING_FINDING_IDS. Material untested requirements and documented stable-interface gaps that can change pass/fail are REVISE. MEDIUM blocks when it can change solver pass/fail or compliance with a documented stable public interface.
Instruction owns the work request; delegated protocol/schema docs are legitimate. Every tested behavior must be discoverable; every material requirement needs a meaningful assertion.

findings.criterion: Published last_run.warehouse.event_count and ops-report.inventory.event_count must equal COUNT(*) of click_event; the verifier must bind that equality, not only cross-file positivity.
findings.why_it_matters: The binding contract defines those integers as COUNT(*) of click_event in catalog.sqlite and requires catalog.available true when loaded. The test only checks that the two JSON integers match, are > 0, and catalog.available is true. A solver can hardcode matching positives (for example 1 and 1) without reading the catalog and still score 1. That is a documented stable public interface the suite does not enforce, so pass/fail can diverge from the published schema.
findings.minimal_remediation: Q2: in the ops-report test (or a sibling), open /app/sessions/warehouse/catalog.sqlite and assert both warehouse.event_count and inventory.event_count equal SELECT COUNT(*) FROM click_event. Keep catalog.available is True. Do not grade extra desk keys.
findings.regression_risk: Low. sqlite3 is stdlib; catalog.sqlite ships under the transferred /app/sessions tree. Wrong COUNT(*) implementations that currently pass will start failing, which is the intended contract.

findings.criterion: --input secondary tie-break (tenant_id, user_id, event_id) is specified but not uniquely exercised.
findings.why_it_matters: Event-time sort is F2P-tested with a reversed two-time file. The permutation P2P uses three different users at one timestamp, so per-user event_ids cannot reveal secondary key order. A stable sort-by-time-only implementation still passes. Not blocking: equal-time same-key order is a refinement of an already graded --input time sort, and no current fixture makes the secondary keys observable.
findings.minimal_remediation: Optional: same-user same-timestamp permutation asserting event_ids follow event_id ascending.

findings.criterion: Closed-session uniqueness (no duplicate identity+interval rows) is stated but not asserted.
findings.why_it_matters: Tests inspect the first matching close or byte-digest a deterministic double-emit. Duplicate closes of the same interval can still pass. Advisory: positive gap-close semantics and idempotent clean-baseline digests are already graded; uniqueness is a negative cardinality constraint.
findings.minimal_remediation: Optional: assert unique (tenant_id, user_id, start_ms, end_ms) in sessions.jsonl after a gap-close run.

findings.criterion: test_p2p_config_keys is a vacuous preservation check because autouse rewrites processor.json first.
findings.why_it_matters: The fixture writes the three knobs, then the test reads the same path. Agent edits to the shipped default file cannot fail this test. Gap/lateness/duration F2P/P2P mutations already honor the knobs, so this is advisory vacuous P2P rather than an untested requirement.
findings.minimal_remediation: Optional: read keys before rewriting, or drop the vacuous P2P.

findings.criterion: Non-enterprise catalog plans must keep processor.json session_gap_ms; only enterprise overlay is exercised.
findings.why_it_matters: t01 enterprise 45000 vs watermark idle is a meaningful overlay check. A solver who applies 45000 to every catalog plan (standard/internal) would still pass that test; holdout tenants are not in the catalog so they still pin default 30000. Advisory branch coverage, not a hidden requirement.
findings.minimal_remediation: Optional: one standard catalog tenant (for example t00) in the same watermark-idle shape asserting end_ms uses processor.json gap.

findings.criterion: Malformed/rejected lines must not update max_observed; that isolation is not directly asserted.
findings.why_it_matters: Reject tests check side output membership, not journal watermark after mixed malformed lines. Wrong watermark updates from rejects could still pass. Advisory: valid-observation journal tests already pin the formula on clean feeds.
findings.minimal_remediation: Optional: after sample_late_and_reject, assert journal max_observed ignores o4 and the invalid JSON line.

findings.criterion: warehouse line-count >= 10000 is an unpublished numeric floor; leave-alone is already SHA-256 graded.
findings.why_it_matters: Neither instruction nor contract states 10000 lines. A contract-compliant solver who leaves the dump untouched still passes. The floor does not reject a valid solve and is weaker than the SHA check for rewrites. Advisory undocumented threshold, not a blocking phantom.
findings.minimal_remediation: Optional: drop the 10k floor and rely on SHA-256, or document production-scale size in the contract if the floor is intended.

findings.criterion: Successful --empty-check must rewrite last_run.json and ops-report.json; only a non-empty --input path is asserted.
findings.why_it_matters: Empty-check tests cover empty session/late files and no journal; they do not read the desk artifacts. Skipping ops refresh on --empty-check still passes those tests. Advisory path gap; the published fields are already required on another successful-run path (and Q4-B01 covers the COUNT(*) meaning).
findings.minimal_remediation: Optional: after --empty-check, assert last_run.json and ops-report.json were rewritten with the same catalog fields.

do_not_change: Event-time gap, duration, lateness, and watermark-before-update rules in session-contract.md
CLI exit 2 before mutation for unknown flags and missing --input/--feed/--empty-check
Reject identification by event_id (not detail tokens)
Journal seq/nondecreasing/raw negative watermark and restart snapshot behavior
Python run-sessions entrypoint and binding contract path
next_gate: Q2 Verifier Coverage Repairer to bind COUNT(*) on last_run/ops-report, then refreeze and re-run Q4

REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.requirement: Repair the existing Python processor; do not move session logic to another language or discard the journal protocol
Unknown flags exit 2 before mutating journal, opens, or outputs (including with --reset-output)
Omitting --input/--feed/--empty-check exits 2 before journal/output touch
--input orders by event_time_ms before session assignment
--input tie-breaks equal times by (tenant_id, user_id, event_id) ascending
--feed preserves file/arrival order so out-of-order event times remain
--reset-output truncates sessions/late/rejects and must not clear journal or in-flight sessions
--empty-check or zero-event input leaves sessions.jsonl and late.jsonl empty and does not advance the journal
Session key is (tenant_id, user_id); equal user_id must not merge across tenants
On-time gap close uses event time; end_ms = last_event_time_ms + session_gap_ms; intervals are half-open
max_session_duration_ms closes then opens a new session when accepting would exceed the span
watermark_ms = max_observed_event_time_ms - allowed_lateness_ms; journal records raw (possibly negative) integer; lateness compares max(0, W)
Late/on-time decision uses watermark from before this event updates max_observed; then journal and watermark-close
Journaled watermark_ms is non-decreasing across observations and restarts; seq starts at 1 and increments per parsed observation including unchanged watermark
Late-but-allowed events join the open session when event_time is in [start_ms, last+gap); last_event_time_ms updates only if greater
Too-late events go to late.jsonl with reason TOO_LATE and comparison watermark_ms
After watermark update, close open sessions where last_event_time_ms + session_gap_ms <= W
Closed session JSONL has tenant_id, user_id, start_ms, end_ms, event_ids, event_count==len(event_ids), end_ms>start_ms
Do not emit duplicate closes for the same session identity and interval
Reload journal and open_sessions.json so in-flight sessions continue and seq/watermark remain consistent
From a clean journal, a second identical --reset-output run keeps SHA-256 of sessions.jsonl and late.jsonl

Malformed JSON, missing fields, wrong types, empty ids, and negative event_time_ms fail closed into rejects.jsonl as REJECT_MALFORMED; empty payload is accepted; continue later lines; identify event_id when it is a string
Rejected malformed lines do not update max_observed / watermark
processor.json gap, allowed_lateness, and max_session_duration are honored; lateness and max duration always come from that file
Catalog-backed enterprise tenants overlay session_gap_ms=45000
Non-enterprise catalog plans keep processor.json session_gap_ms
Each successful run including --empty-check rewrites last_run.json and ops-report.json from the warehouse catalog
last_run.warehouse.event_count and ops-report.inventory.event_count equal COUNT(*) of click_event; ops-report.catalog.available is true when catalog loaded
Leave /app/sessions/warehouse production click dump in place
Documented output paths under /app/sessions/output are used
Crash-consistent snapshot/journal writes; UTF-8 JSONL without BOM; create parent directories

PHANTOM_TEST_CONTRACTS: test_p2p_warehouse_at_least_10k unpublished 10000-line floor (advisory; SHA-256 already enforces leave-alone; does not reject a contract-compliant solver)
UNTESTED_REQUIREMENTS: last_run.warehouse.event_count and ops-report.inventory.event_count equal catalog COUNT(*) (material; Q4-B01)
No duplicate closes for the same identity+interval (advisory; Q4-A02)
Non-enterprise catalog plan keeps processor.json gap (advisory; Q4-A04)
Rejected lines do not update watermark (advisory; Q4-A05)
Crash-consistent temp+rename journal/snapshot and UTF-8 no-BOM (advisory; not Harbor-observable without crash injection)
role_output.DELEGATED_CONTRACT_CHECK: session-contract.md is legitimate CLI/path/schema/event-time/journal/restart documentation explicitly bound by instruction.md. oncall.md and processor-bounce.log are incident evidence, not an acceptance checklist. processor.json and catalog.sqlite are inherited config/state. Material goals (repair processor, CLI, event-time sessions, journal, rejects, ops artifacts, catalog overlay, leave warehouse) remain in instruction.md.

F2P_P2P_WALK.f2p: Unknown flags, missing source, empty/zero-event, event-time gap, input time-sort, tenant isolation, journal seq/prefix/nondecreasing/negative watermark, too-late schema, idempotent digest, restart, config gap/lateness, holdout gap+idle close, feed order, reset-output. These are defect-shaped relative to the incident log.
F2P_P2P_WALK.p2p: Warehouse SHA leave-alone, python3 launcher, contract formula string, output parents, late-allowed join, max-duration close, reject classes by event_id, ops field presence, enterprise overlay. test_p2p_config_keys is vacuous (autouse rewrite). test_p2p_input_tie_break_stable is permutation-stable but not a unique secondary-key check. No circular oracle: tests drive run-sessions and parse outputs.
F2P_P2P_WALK.bypass: Hardcoded last_run/ops-report matching positives bypass COUNT(*) (Q4-B01). Overlay cannot be bypassed by skipping catalog if t01 would otherwise watermark-close at 30000.

OUTPUT_INTERFACE_WALK.sessions.jsonl: schema fields, event_count, half-open end_ms, holdout/gap values
OUTPUT_INTERFACE_WALK.rejects.jsonl: REJECT_MALFORMED, event_id including empty string, line_no/detail presence; not detail tokens
OUTPUT_INTERFACE_WALK.watermark.journal: seq, max_observed, raw watermark_ms, prefix append, nondecreasing
OUTPUT_INTERFACE_WALK.open_sessions.json: per-key event_ids/start_ms/last_event_time_ms; max_observed field not separately asserted
OUTPUT_INTERFACE_WALK.last_run.json: warehouse.event_count present and positive; COUNT(*) unbound
OUTPUT_INTERFACE_WALK.ops-report.json: catalog.available true; inventory.event_count matches warehouse.event_count; COUNT(*) unbound
OUTPUT_INTERFACE_WALK.catalog.sqlite: required for overlay and ops refresh; COUNT(*) not queried by verifier
